name: ICT Card (Intra-Corporate Transfer)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires at least 6 months' prior employment within the same corporate group before the transfer.
This requires transferring as a manager, specialist, or trainee employee under an assignment letter from the group.
This requires an assignment period of more than 90 days — shorter transfers use short-term mobility rules instead of the ICT Card.

evidence_required.document: Assignment letter confirming intra-group transfer terms and duration
Proof of 6+ months' prior employment within the group

outcome.duration_length: up to 3 years (managers/specialists), up to 1 year (trainees)

notes: Deliberately terminal in this dataset — ICT time does NOT count toward permanent residence, since it's a temporary posting rather than an immigration route in the settlement sense. This is a genuine structural outlier: leads_to_pr false and switchable_to empty, similar to UK Youth Mobility and UK High Potential Individual, but for the opposite reason (those are genuinely time-limited early-career routes; this is a corporate mobility instrument that was never meant to lead anywhere). 6-month cooling-off period required before a new ICT card can be issued — not yet modeled as a distinct field. EU short-term mobility (up to 90 days in other member states without a new permit) and the separate Mobile ICT Card (for stays over 90 days in a second EU state) are related but distinct instruments, not encoded as separate routes here — flagged as a scope decision, not an oversight.
